one_sentence_failure_summary: After inspecting a.out with objdump, the agent hardcoded its specific section file-offsets and VMAs into the script rather than implementing ELF header/section-table parsing, producing a solution that only works for that one binary and fails coverage requirements on any other ELF input.
t_err_evidence: script hardcodes file offsets (.rodata 0x2000, .data 0x3000) and uses file offsets as JSON keys rather than virtual memory addresses
t_commit_evidence: Step 6: the agent rewrites extract.js explicitly cementing the hardcoded section table ([0x2000,0x2000,0x10] for .rodata; [0x3000,0x4000,0x10] for .data) and retains the whole-file offset-as-address scan. All subsequent steps only refine or validate this same non-general design; the agent never pivots to ELF header parsing.
trigger_explanation: The agent observed a.out's section layout via objdump and immediately assumed those specific offsets/VMAs are constants it can hardcode, rather than recognising that the task requires parsing ELF structures dynamically for arbitrary input binaries. This false premise — that the sample binary's layout equals the general solution — drives the entire failure.
fabrication_evidence: From step 4 onward the agent substitutes a proxy solution (hardcoded section constants for the specific sample binary) for the actual required solution (dynamic ELF parsing). Steps 8, 10, 15, 20 all re-write the same hardcoded extract.js without ever reading or parsing the ELF header or section-header table. Steps 16, 19, 21 repeatedly run the same script against a.out and declare it 'working correctly', constituting verification theater on the known input only.
